message.reasoning:
I need to make a decision for the current Monopoly turn.

I have the orange monopoly and $347 cash. I am recalculating the mortgage strategy to build one house on each property.

One house on each orange property costs $300. I must build evenly.

Building one house on each orange property now would leave only $47. That is too risky against a $200 railroad rent from player three. I should mortgage Water Works and Vermont first to build evenly with a larger cushion.

Selling houses would recover $150, but the engine may not allow mortgage or sale during debt resolution. I need to confirm whether I can raise cash after landing on a railroad.

Mortgaging Water Works and Vermont first would bring cash to $472. That leaves $172 after building one house on each orange property. Selling one house plus that remaining cash covers a $200 railroad rent.

I will mortgage Water Works first. The utility monopoly is already broken since Electric Company is mortgaged. I can mortgage Vermont on the next turn or build houses after that.

Mortgaging Vermont will not break the light blue block for player two, since mortgaged properties still count as owned. Building two houses on each orange property would cost $600, which is too much. I must build one house on each property.

I am reconsidering the house plan. Two houses on each orange property would cost $400 and leave only $72 cash, which is too risky against a $200 railroad rent. One house on each property costs $300 and leaves $172, so I will build evenly with one house per property instead.

Standard orange rent values are $14/$70/$200/$550/$750/$950 for St. James, $18/$90/$250/$700/$875/$1050 for Tennessee, and $20/$100/$300/$750/$925/$1100 for New York. Three houses on each property would be devastatingly powerful.

Player four proposed a trade with player three: States and Virginia for Park Place. Player three would then own the pink monopoly, while player four would own the dark blue set.

Player four already owns States and Virginia, so they can complete the dark blue monopoly. Player three can also finish the pink set. I cannot block this trade directly because I no longer own those properties.

Player four has $744 cash, which is enough to build houses on dark blue. Dark blue houses cost $200 each, so they can develop quickly. I need to get houses on orange as fast as possible before they build on dark blue and pink.
